verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion capsule has splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off San Diego and describe it as safe/perfect.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: timestamps 'April 10, 2026'; R2: 'splashed down... on Friday night' (context April 10); R3: 'April 10, 2026 implied in updates'; R4: 'Updated April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm splashdown on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. ET'; R3: '8:07 p.m. EDT'; R4: '8:07 p.m. Eastern Time'; R7: '8:07 p.m. ET'; R8: '8:07 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely state 8:07 p.m. ET/EDT for splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft carried four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'four Artemis II astronauts'; R2: 'four astronauts aboard the Orion'; R3: 'four astronauts'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm four astronauts on Orion.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft landed after a 10-day mission around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day trip to the moon'; R2: '10-day mission'; R3: 'approximate 10-day mission around the Moon'; R4: '10-day mission'; R5: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe it as a 10-day mission around the moon, despite precise duration being 9 days + due to counting launch as day 1.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams including the USS John P. Murtha were positioned to assist the crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery ship, USS John P. Murtha, which was positioned about 2,000 yards away'; R3: 'recovery team aboard the USS John P. Murtha'; R6: 'USS John P. Murtha was staged... ready to recover'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm recovery teams and USS John P. Murtha positioned for crew assistance.

verifications.claim: The spacecraft was the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion spacecraft', 'Orion capsule'; R2: 'Orion space capsule'; R3: 'Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: All sources identify the spacecraft as Orion capsule/spacecraft.

verifications.claim: The recovery team was the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery ship, USS John P. Murtha'; R2: 'recovery crew from the USS John P Murtha'; R3: 'recovery team aboard the USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe USS John P. Murtha as the recovery ship with teams/crew aboard/from it, but do not state the team 'was' the ship itself; broader description.

verifications.claim: The crew consisted of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Reid Wiseman... Christina Koch and Victor Glover... Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover... Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and... Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Sources exactly list the four crew members with correct affiliations.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'all four members of the crew were "feeling great, happy to be home"'; R2: 'all four astronauts in good health'; R3: 'safely extracted'; R4: 'safely returned'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm safe extraction and recovery of crew, all in good condition.
